trust_decision.summary: Whether a request may reach a spawn-capable / host-secret route, or any /api/* route at all, is decided by the Next.js proxy: first by config.matcher (which decides whether dashboardGuard.proxy runs) and then by isLocalRequest, which trusts the attacker-controlled Host header (and Origin only when the client chooses to send it) instead of a secret.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names a local-only gate bypassed by Host header spoofing, so the first grep lands on isLocalRequest and the LOCAL_ONLY_PATHS gate that calls it at src/dashboardGuard.js:92-96; the matcher that decides whether that code runs at all lives in a different file.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: src/proxy.js is a one-line re-export of dashboardGuard.proxy, so an engineer who fixes the Host-header check inside dashboardGuard.js reads the second file as plumbing and never widens config.matcher, leaving /api/version/*, /api/oauth/* and /api/v1* outside the guard entirely.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Unauthenticated loopback traffic must keep reaching both the LLM API and the pre-login reads: /v1 and /v1beta are used by local CLI tools with no dashboard session, and the login page reads requireLogin before any credential exists, so a fix that makes the loopback allowance token-only everywhere (or deny-by-default without an allow-list) breaks local tools and the login page.

O6_input_shapes: Pathname spelling for the same handler: /v1 and /v1beta rewritten to /api/v1 by next.config.mjs:54-61, versus /api/v1 and /api/v1beta called directly; matching is p === pathname || pathname.startsWith(p + '/'), so /v1/v1 (next.config.mjs:43-49) and /api/v1beta also count

Host header shapes: 'localhost:20128' (port split off at src/dashboardGuard.js:50), '[::1]' (brackets stripped at src/dashboardGuard.js:50), '127.0.0.1', and any spoofed non-loopback spelling that defeats the gate
Origin present vs absent: an omitted Origin is accepted (src/dashboardGuard.js:58-63), so a non-browser client needs no Origin at all; a cross-site browser form post does send one
Credential shapes for the remote LLM API: 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' and 'x-api-key: <key>', Bearer taking precedence (fix.diff:42-46)
Method shapes for the same route family: GET (auto-import, mcp sse) and POST (mcp message, tailscale-install, version/update, version/shutdown)

O7_producer.where: src/shared/utils/machineId.js:10-19 derives the CLI token as sha256(machineId + '9r-cli-auth')[0:16], cached per process at src/dashboardGuard.js:9-13 and re-derived in two other places: src/app/api/cli-tools/cowork-settings/route.js:18-22 (injects the header into generated MCP configs) and cli/src/cli/api/client.js:17-28 (the CLI's own copy)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: POST /api/auth/login decides 'is this request coming in over the tunnel?' from the Host header, so a tunneled client that sends Host: localhost logs in even when settings.tunnelDashboardAccess is false — the same spoofable-locality decision the advisory is about, in another file, untouched by the fix
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Login is the public auth endpoint that has to be reachable from anywhere, and the tunnel-dashboard restriction reads as a separate dashboard policy rather than the spawn-capable local-only gate the advisory names.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: one directory tree away (src/app/api/auth vs src/), 1 file from the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The /dashboard tunnel block also compares the Host header against settings.tunnelUrl/tailscaleUrl, so a spoofed Host skips the 'dashboard access via tunnel is disabled' redirect; the fix leaves this branch exactly as it was
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a redirect policy for dashboard pages, not an access gate, and the route still falls through to the JWT check three lines later, so a solver reads the Host comparison as a UX affordance.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~35 lines from the local-only gate

O8_uncovered_routes.route: POST /api/tunnel/tailscale-start-daemon (and its siblings /api/tunnel/tailscale-login, /api/tunnel/tailscale-enable, /api/tunnel/enable, /api/tunnel/disable) spawn host processes - tailscaled with a request-supplied sudo password, or cloudflared - yet are only session-auth-gated and never added to LOCAL_ONLY_PATHS, while the fix's own comment calls LOCAL_ONLY_PATHS the list for routes that spawn processes or read host secrets
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: They sit behind dashboard/CLI auth already, and the tunnel feature has to be operable from a dashboard that may itself be reached over a tunnel, so loopback-only looks like it would break the feature.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: src/app/api/tunnel/ vs src/dashboardGuard.js — 2 directories, and the spawn is two layers deeper in src/lib/tunnel/tailscale.js:5,525

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A third 'auto-import from another IDE's local credential store' route (Windsurf / VS Code Copilot) beside the cursor and kiro pairs
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The tree already ships cursor/import + cursor/auto-import and kiro/import + kiro/auto-import as two parallel families, so a maintainer adding one more IDE copies auto-import and forgets that only the auto-import half reads host files and needs LOCAL_ONLY_PATHS.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second config-writer that embeds the x-9r-cli-token header into generated client configs
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This file already re-derives the CLI token and injects it for localhost /api/mcp/ entries; every new local-only route that a generated client must reach needs the same injection, and a maintainer writing another writer would copy these ~5 lines and the cached token value.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A process-spawning host-maintenance route (restart, repair, log-collect, install-binary) that is auth-gated but not local-only
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: version/update and version/shutdown already call killAppProcesses/spawnUpdaterAndExit next to tailscale-install doing the same for tailscaled, so 'add another maintenance action' lands in the same shape and the local-only question repeats.

O9_family: access-control bypass by spoofed identity (CWE-290 authentication bypass by spoofing, CWE-807 reliance on untrusted inputs in a security decision, CWE-306 missing authentication for critical function); specifically an incomplete fix of the earlier loopback-only gate

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Tighten the locality test itself - reject non-loopback Host more strictly, parse X-Forwarded-For, or accept the socket address - which is still header/proxy-derived, and leave config.matcher in src/proxy.js plus the two duplicated Host comparisons untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: src/app/api/auth/login/route.js:25-38: password login falls back to the default '123456' (or INITIAL_PASSWORD) when no hash is stored - a credential-policy issue, not this advisory.
src/dashboardGuard.js:81-86: requireLogin === false makes isAuthenticated() true for every PROTECTED path, which is a documented setting rather than the local gate.
src/app/api/tunnel/tailscale-install/route.js:25,44: a request-supplied sudo password is handed to installTailscale - host command execution, but the advisory's property only covers who may reach it.
unverified: Repo size in MB: no shell was available this session, so tiny_repo (<5 MB) and giant_repo (>1.5 GB) were not assessed and left unflagged; the tree includes a gitbook docs subapp, 126 route files and monaco, so it is unlikely to be under 5 MB of source.
